sentences: Revolving credit utilization is by far the most important driver of default risk, and the risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use climbs, most sharply above about 0.7.
Past delinquencies are the next most important driver: having at least one delinquency on the file raises the predicted risk, with a moderate effect.
Annual income is also a moderate driver, and higher income lowers the predicted risk, with the largest drop among applicants whose income is above about 84,000 dollars.
Length of credit history has a weaker effect, with longer histories associated with lower risk, though the size of this effect is uncertain.
The effect of utilization is about the same across different credit history lengths, so the two do not interact in any practically meaningful way.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio, the two application attributes, and the age and inquiry features matter at all, since their effects cannot be resolved at this sample size.
Recent credit inquiries hardly matter to the model's predictions.
